comments.text_zh: 你持的是凯恩斯主义观点。这个议题很难用超过一句金句的方式讨论，但这两个视频把哈耶克观点解释得很好：[VIDEO] [LINK] 如果你还没看过，非常值得一看。简而言之，相反/哈耶克的观点主张，税收是把资源从有利润/有效率的主体那里夺走，再重新分配给没有利润/无效率的主体。我们在银行救助中极端地看到了这一点，在更具争议的个体再分配中则微观地看到了这一点。如果你接受这一点——即“有利润”与“有效率”相关，反过来也相关，尽管这种相关性并不完美——那么税收就不是什么增加福祉的罗宾汉式行为，而是一种把经济中有效率的部门——那些即使在艰难时期也能实现盈利的部门——的腿绑到已经溺水者身上的举动。
comments.text: You take the Keynesian view. It's difficult to discuss this in more than a soundbite, but the Hayekian view is well explained by these two videos: [VIDEO] [LINK] Well worth watching if you haven't seen them. In short, the opposite/Hayekian view contends that taxation is seizure of resources from profitable/efficient entities and redistribution towards unprofitable/inefficient entities. We saw this in extremis in the bank bailout, and more controversially in microcosm with individual redistribution. If you accept this -- that "profitable" correlates with "efficient", and conversely, though the correlation is not perfect -- then taxation is not a Robin Hood sort of thing that increases well being, but rather a move that ties the legs of the efficient sectors of the economy -- those that can post a profit even in tough times -- to those that are already underwater.

comments.text_zh: 这是凯恩斯主义和货币主义对预算的看法。其想法是，如果你要平衡预算（他们如今往往认为这从来都不是什么好主意），那也应该在整个经济周期的起伏中实现平衡。假设一个经济周期又开始了，而政府不知怎么地在收入进来之前没把那笔额外的钱全花掉，于是就有了盈余。可繁荣之后必然跟着萧条，不管别人怎么跟你说，等下一轮开始时就是这样。凯恩斯主张，在萧条期应该花钱，以维持总需求，让经济复苏。所以在这段时间里你要运行赤字。如果考虑平衡预算，他们可能会主张你应该把短期得失也考虑进去来平衡它。如果你感兴趣，这个视频是了解关于经济周期的两种不同观点的一种有趣且非常准确的方式：[VIDEO] 顺便说一句，在这个视频里我站哈耶克 :)
comments.text: This is a Keynesian and Monetarist view of budgets. The idea is that IF you balance the budget (they often don't think this is ever a great idea anymore) then it should be balanced over the ups and downs of the business cycle. So let's say a business cycle starts up again and somehow the government doesn't spend all that extra money before it comes in and there is surplus. Now booms are followed by an inevitable bust no matter what anyone tells you when the next one starts up. Keynes argued that you should spend during busts to keep aggregate demand up and let the economy recover. So you run a deficit during this time. If you consider a balanced budget then they might argue that you should balance it with consideration to short term gains and losses. If you're interested this video is a fun and very accurate way to learn about two different views of the business cycle: [VIDEO] For the record I'm with Hayek in this video :)

comments.text: He's talking about the satellite photo story from a while back in which Greeks had many more (taxable) private pools than were reported to the government. [LINK] The question though is whether "more efficient tax collection" is really the cure for Greece's ailments. It really boils down to whether you think a centralized government can better allocate your dollars to your benefit, or whether you can. You could certainly make an argument that people would free ride and/or greatly underestimate the benefit that spending 10 cents of each dollar on (say) the military or roads would provide, and this furthermore justifies taking that 10 cents by force as part of the price of membership in a community. However, I personally find it less persuasive to argue that centralized allocation programs will produce greater wealth than distributed ones. A remote government simply doesn't have all the information and can't know your preferences. One thing I find interesting is that many people can come to fairly good agreement on what the problem is (bad economy, low unemployment, etc.) but disagree very dramatically on what the solution should be. frossie is likely a Keynesian and rick888 is probably a Hayekian; in my experience, Keynesianism is in the water supply and the "default belief" for most college graduates, but most entrepreneurs tend to end up Hayekian: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 你看，我其实是主张社会安全网的。我认为政府的角色可以简单地定义为“确保社会的最低期望得到满足”，并且充分认识到这些期望（自来水供应、医疗进步等）会随时间提高，也因地而异。我完全支持把政府职能下放到街区层面——你们很多人知道，我总体上支持更多的去中心化。然而，即使像我这样的人也能说，这篇文章远远不足以支撑它那个大胆的标题。它主要是对 Keynes 及其概念的颂歌。此外，它还包含一些谬误：但是，如果政府承担服务成本，为什么不自己提供呢？如果无论如何都要为所做的事情付钱，为什么要花时间和金钱组建合作关系并监督其结果？因为当提供者竞争时，质量上升、成本下降。（另一方面，当购买者竞争时，成本上升，这就是单一支付者体系能降低成本的原因。）这些问题的答案集中在私营企业更高的效率，以及由此带来的公私合作成本节约。然而，关于公私合作在基础设施投资中应用的研究，几乎不支持这种假定的成本节约。把 VA 和 Medicare 比较一下。然而，除了道路使用者之外，许多人也能从中受益——仅举几例，沿线的企业。如果其通行费减少了交通……这些企业会和使用者一起受损。

comments.text: Not if you're invested in it. Not if you want to see blockchain technology used to replace the DTCC. Not if you think there are potentially extreme differences between crime (laws enforced by power) and justice (what is ethically right or wrong). The people who invest in crypto are rent-seeking parasites hoping to extract value while incidentally providing liquidity to the Chinese miners blowing non trivial amounts of co2 in the air. The people who transact in crypto are actually building it and working towards the crypto dream of alternative currency. It's important to understand that when a company sells a stock, they get money that they can then use to grow themselves. So there is generally some of the principal "retained" in a unit of stock, particularly because the unit of stock also creates a legal relationship with the company. By definition all crypto starts from a miner, so when you buy a unit of crypto, you are transferring money directly to the miner. So the unit of crypto retains none of the principal investment. That is an absolute terrifying property. I am not quite sure what I think of ETH yet, since it's a little different, but BTC is straight bad for the environment.
